title: Tend your own soul first.
subtitle: Responsibility for yourself, without abandoning others

row.title: reform yourself
sub: and still change what you see

then: Ibn Kathir says Allah tells the believers to {idea}reform themselves first{/idea}, and that one who does so is not harmed by others' wrongdoing, even relatives. Abu Bakr once stood and warned people they were {trap}reading this verse the wrong way{/trap}, quoting the Prophet ﷺ: if people see evil and do not change it, punishment may cover them all.
now: You get absorbed in what everyone else is doing wrong: your sibling's choices, your colleague's shortcuts, the comments under a post. Meanwhile your own prayer is slipping. Start with {idea}your own heart{/idea}. That is not the same as {trap}shrugging at wrong{/trap}. It is fixing yourself so your voice carries.
old: Either I focus on others' wrongs, or I mind my own business completely.
new: I reform myself first, and from there I can still help others kindly.
try: Before commenting on anyone else's faults today, fix one small thing in your own routine.

title: Even for a relative, we will not sell our oath.
subtitle: Witnessing a dying person's wishes faithfully

picture.label: At a deathbed on a journey

then: The verse covers a hard moment: death approaching on a journey, a will being made, two witnesses present. If doubted, they swear after the prayer: {idea}we will not exchange this for any gain, even for a near relative, and we will not hide the testimony of Allah.{/idea} Ibn Kathir notes it is called Allah's testimony {reward}to show how much it is worth.{/reward}
now: Your uncle is dying. He tells you, quietly, what he wants done with his savings. Later, the family argues, and your side would gain if you remembered it a little differently. {trap}A small bend for family{/trap} feels almost loyal. The verse says: {idea}not even for family.{/idea}
old: Bending the truth a little to help my family is loyalty.
new: What I witness is a trust from Allah. I will not trade it, even for family.
try: If you are holding anyone's wishes or words in trust, write them down accurately today.

title: When witnesses cheat, the rightful step up.
subtitle: Correcting false testimony with truthful testimony
then: If the witnesses are found to have {trap}cheated or stolen from the estate{/trap}, Ibn Kathir explains, two of the nearest rightful heirs swear in their place. Their oath includes a line that matters: {idea}we have not transgressed, or we would be among the wrongdoers.{/idea} Even the correction must be honest.
now: Someone lied about you at work, and you finally get your chance to set the record straight. It is tempting to {trap}add a few extra charges while you are at it{/trap}. The heirs in this verse swear they have not overstepped. {idea}Your correction has to be as true as you wish theirs had been.{/idea}
old: Once someone wrongs me, I am free to say whatever I like about them.
new: Even when correcting a lie, I must not cross into one myself.
try: Next time you tell the story of someone who wronged you, tell only what you know for sure.

title: A system that makes honesty more likely.
subtitle: Why oaths and checks protect the truth
then: Ibn Kathir explains the wisdom: swearing by Allah, whom they revere, and the chance that {trap}the heirs' oaths may overturn theirs{/trap}, both push witnesses to tell the truth as it is. The verse ends with the core: {idea}fear Allah and listen.{/idea}
now: The family business with no written records. The group trip money that "we will sort out later". Good people still forget and still get tempted. {idea}Writing it down, having a witness, being accountable{/idea} is not distrust. {reward}It protects everyone, including you.{/reward}
old: Asking for records or witnesses means I do not trust people.
new: Clear checks plus fear of Allah protect everyone's honesty, including mine.
try: Write down one money arrangement you have with family or friends and share it with them.

title: Even the messengers will say: we have no knowledge.
subtitle: The Day when only Allah knows what was hidden

row.title: I know their hearts
sub: I can tell what they meant

then: Allah will gather the messengers and ask how their people responded. Mujahid and others said they answer {trap}we have no knowledge{/trap} out of the awe of that Day. Ibn 'Abbas explained it as respect: {idea}our knowledge saw only what people did outwardly; You know what was in their hearts.{/idea}
now: You are sure you know why your friend did not invite you, why your sister-in-law said that, why that man at the masjid frowned. The best of humanity will say {idea}we only saw the outside.{/idea} Maybe {trap}you do not know their hearts either.{/trap}
old: I can usually tell what people really meant.
new: I see what people do. Only Allah knows why.
try: Think of one person whose motives you have judged. Give them one good excuse today.

title: Remember My favour on you and your mother.
subtitle: Every miracle of 'Isa, by Allah's permission
then: On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will remind 'Isa of His favours: {reward}Jibril's support, speaking as a baby to clear his mother's name{/reward}, the Book and wisdom, the clay bird, healing, raising the dead. Every one is followed by {idea}by My permission.{/idea} Ibn Kathir notes that Allah also saved him from those who rejected him and tried to kill him.
now: The promotion, the recovery after surgery, the child who finally started talking. You worked hard, the doctors were good. But {idea}by His permission{/idea} belongs after each one. List them. {reward}Remembering favours is how gratitude starts.{/reward}
old: My successes come from my effort and skill.
new: Every good thing I do happens by Allah's permission, even the miracles of prophets.
try: Write a list of five favours in your life and add by Allah's permission after each.

title: Allah put faith in their hearts, and they answered.
subtitle: The disciples' response to inspiration

row.title: Allah inspired
sub: believe in Me and My messenger

then: This is another favour on 'Isa: {reward}companions who believed with him.{/reward} Al-Hasan al-Basri said Allah inspired them, and As-Suddi said {idea}He put it in their hearts{/idea}. They replied: {reward}we believe, so bear witness that we are Muslims.{/reward}
now: That moment you suddenly felt the pull to pray again, after months. That verse that hit you at a funeral. You might think you decided. {idea}Allah placed it in your heart.{/idea} Your part is to answer like the disciples did: {reward}I believe, bear witness.{/reward}
old: My faith is something I built on my own.
new: Allah puts faith in the heart. My part is to answer it.
try: Thank Allah today for the moment He first turned your heart toward Him, if you can remember it.

title: Can your Lord send us a table from heaven?
subtitle: The request that gave this surah its name
then: This is the story of al-Ma'idah, the table that names the surah. Some scholars said the disciples were poor and wanted daily food to help them worship. Ibn Kathir explains 'Isa's reply: {idea}be mindful of Allah, do not ask for this, for it may become a trial for you; trust Allah for your provision.{/idea}
now: You pray: if You really hear me, give me a sign. The job offer, the test result, a message from them. {trap}Asking for proof can turn into a test you might fail.{/trap} 'Isa's answer still works: {idea}be mindful of Allah, and trust Him with your provision.{/idea}
old: If Allah showed me a clear sign, my faith would be strong.
new: Trust comes first. Demanding signs can become its own trial.
try: Make one dua today without asking for a sign, just trusting that He heard.
